config.title: Star Rating Component

intro.title: Star Rating Component
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive star rating component that allows users to select and display ratings. You'll learn how to manage component state in React using the useState hook to track the current rating. The component will use TypeScript to define proper types for props and state, ensuring type safety. You'll implement click handlers to update the rating when users click on stars, and conditionally render filled or empty stars based on the current rating value.
intro.usecase: Star rating components are essential interactive UI elements found across modern web applications. You'll implement them in e-commerce product pages for customer reviews, in streaming platforms for content ratings, and in feedback forms for user surveys. As a developer, you'll build these components to capture user sentiment, display aggregated ratings, and enhance user engagement with intuitive visual feedback. Mastering this pattern prepares you for common frontend tasks like handling user input, managing component state, and creating reusable UI controls.

objectives: Define a TypeScript interface to specify the props structure for a reusable StarRating component.
Implement useState hook to manage the active rating state within the component.
Apply array iteration to generate star elements based on a maximum rating value.
Utilize conditional rendering to display either filled or empty star icons.
Construct click event handlers to update the rating state when stars are clicked.
Use inline styles or CSS classes to visually represent the selected rating state.
Execute conditional logic to compare each star's index against the current rating for display decisions.
Return a structured JSX element containing the interactive star rating interface.
Control component behavior by passing and accessing props like maxStars and initialRating.
Invoke the StarRating component within a parent component with specific configuration props.
Modify the rating state in response to user interactions while maintaining TypeScript type safety.
Apply React component composition patterns to integrate the StarRating into a larger UI structure.

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'. This is the foundation for building React components with state.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode:

steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a valid import statement for React and useState at the top of your file.
successCriteria: The import statement must import React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core library and the useState hook for managing component state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import isn't quite complete. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the StarRating component function
steps.instruction: Create a function component named StarRating that returns JSX.Element. Place it below the imports.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to specify the return type as JSX.Element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A StarRating component function is created with the correct return type.
successCriteria: The component is named StarRating, returns JSX.Element, and is placed after the imports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the StarRating component function with the correct TypeScript return type.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named exactly 'StarRating' and returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you've named it 'StarRating' and specified the return type as JSX.Element.

steps.title: Define the component props interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named StarRatingProps above your component function to define the props your StarRating component will accept. The interface should have a required maxRating property of type number and an optional onRatingChange property of type function that takes a number parameter and returns void.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define properties with their types. Remember to make onRatingChange optional with the '?' modifier.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an interface named StarRatingProps with maxRating: number and optional onRatingChange?: (rating: number) => void properties defined.
successCriteria: The interface must be named StarRatingProps, include maxRating as a required number property, and include onRatingChange as an optional function property that takes a number parameter and returns void.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the StarRatingProps interface with the correct properties and types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you have both required maxRating (number) and optional onRatingChange (function taking number and returning void) properties defined in your StarRatingProps interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition doesn't match the requirements. Make sure you create an interface named StarRatingProps with maxRating: number and onRatingChange?: (rating: number) => void.

steps.title: Add props parameter to StarRating with type annotation
steps.instruction: Add a props parameter to the StarRating component function and annotate it with the StarRatingProps interface type.
steps.hint: The props parameter should be typed with the interface you defined earlier. For example: `function StarRating(props: StarRatingProps) { ... }`
steps.expectedOutcome: The StarRating component function should accept a props parameter typed as StarRatingProps.
successCriteria: StarRating function has a props parameter
props parameter is typed with StarRatingProps
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the typed props parameter to your component. This ensures TypeScript will validate that the component receives the correct props.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added both the props parameter AND typed it with the StarRatingProps interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have a properly typed props parameter. Check that you've added `props: StarRatingProps` as the function parameter.

steps.title: Initialize rating state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside the StarRating component, declare a rating state variable using useState. Initialize it to 0 and specify its type as number.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to provide the generic type parameter <number>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a rating state variable initialized to 0 with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: Declare rating state with useState
Initialize to 0
Specify type as number
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the rating state with proper TypeScript typing. This gives us a place to store the current star rating value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with the number type and initializing it to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to declare a rating state variable using useState, initialize it to 0, and specify its type as number.

steps.title: Create handleStarClick handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the StarRating component, create a function named handleStarClick that takes a number parameter (starIndex) and returns void. This function should update the rating state with the starIndex value and call the onRatingChange prop if it exists.
steps.hint: Define the function before the return statement. Use the setRating function from useState to update state. Check if onRatingChange exists before calling it.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleStarClick function is defined inside the component that properly updates the rating state and conditionally calls the onRatingChange callback.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleStarClick, take a number parameter, update the rating state using setRating, and conditionally call onRatingChange with the new rating.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleStarClick handler that updates state and calls the callback when provided.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function properly updates the rating state and conditionally calls onRatingChange if it exists.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleStarClick function is missing or doesn't correctly update state and call the callback. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Return a container div from the component
steps.instruction: Update the StarRating component to return a div element from its function body.
steps.hint: Replace the existing return statement with one that returns a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div element, providing the basic JSX structure for the star rating UI.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element
The div is returned from the function body
The return statement uses JSX syntax
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully set up the basic JSX structure by returning a div element from the StarRating component. This provides the container for your star rating UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element from the component's function body. Check that your return statement uses JSX syntax with angle brackets.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't seem to return a div element. Remember to update the return statement to return a div element using JSX syntax.

steps.title: Create star rendering helper function
steps.instruction: Inside the StarRating component, create a helper function called 'renderStars' that returns an array of JSX elements. The function should take no parameters for now.
steps.hint: Define a function inside your component that returns an empty array (e.g., return []). We'll fill it with stars in the next step.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a 'renderStars' function defined inside your component that returns an empty array.
successCriteria: The code must contain a function named 'renderStars' defined inside the StarRating component. The function should return an array (empty is fine for now).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the helper function that will generate your star elements. Next we'll make it actually create stars based on the maxRating.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a function called 'renderStars' inside the component that returns an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function called 'renderStars' inside your StarRating component that returns an array.

steps.title: Call star rendering function inside the container div
steps.instruction: Inside the container div's JSX, call the star rendering helper function to display the stars.
steps.hint: You can call the helper function directly within the JSX using curly braces, like {renderStars()}.
steps.expectedOutcome: The star rendering function is called inside the container div, making the stars appear in the UI.
successCriteria: Call the renderStars function within the container div's JSX using curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the star rendering function, which will display the stars in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling the renderStars function inside the container div's JSX using curly braces, like {renderStars()}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The star rendering function hasn't been called yet. Inside the container div, add {renderStars()} to display the stars.

steps.title: Add onClick handler to each star
steps.instruction: In the renderStars function, add an onClick handler to each star <span> element that calls handleStarClick with the star's index (i).
steps.hint: Inside the <span> element, add onClick={() => handleStarClick(i)}. This will make each star clickable.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each star in the renderStars function will have an onClick handler that calls handleStarClick with the star's index.
successCriteria: The onClick handler is added to each <span> element inside the renderStars function, calling handleStarClick(i).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added onClick handlers to each star, making them interactive.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the onClick handler might be missing or not correctly calling handleStarClick with the star index.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onClick handler is not correctly added to the star elements. Make sure to add onClick={() => handleStarClick(i)} inside each <span>.

steps.title: Add conditional star styling based on rating
steps.instruction: In the renderStars function, update the style attribute of each star to use a ternary operator that sets the color to 'gold' when the star index is less than or equal to the current rating, and 'gray' otherwise.
steps.hint: Replace the hardcoded color in the style attribute with a ternary expression like: `color: i <= rating ? 'gold' : 'gray'`.
steps.expectedOutcome: The stars will now visually reflect the current rating: filled stars (gold) up to the selected rating, and empty stars (gray) beyond it.
successCriteria: The style attribute uses a ternary operator
The condition compares the star index (i) with the rating state
The color is 'gold' when the condition is true, 'gray' when false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional styling for the stars. The ternary operator dynamically changes the star color based on the current rating.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the conditional styling isn't quite complete. Make sure you're using a ternary operator that compares the star index with the rating state and sets the appropriate colors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional styling isn't implemented correctly. You need to update the style attribute to use a ternary operator that sets 'gold' when i <= rating and 'gray' otherwise.

steps.title: Display current rating text
steps.instruction: Add a span element that displays the current rating value inside the container div, after the stars.
steps.hint: You can add a span element with the text content showing the rating value. Use JSX curly braces to embed the rating state variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now show the numeric rating value next to the stars, allowing users to see the current rating clearly.
successCriteria: Add a span element after the stars in the return statement
Display the rating state variable inside the span using JSX curly braces
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a span element that displays the current rating value. This completes the star rating component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a span element after the stars and included the rating value inside it using curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rating text isn't displaying correctly. Check that you've added a span element after the stars and used {rating} to show the current rating value.
